INTRODUCTIONM
Making comparisons helps you to make a decision. In this lesson you will see how a 4 bit comparator helps circuits make decisions.
Let's begin the lesson on 4 BIT COMPARATOR................................
LESSON MENU
A comparator looks at two inputs and determines if the inputs are the same or different.
DISCUSSION
If the inputs are the same, then we can say A and B are equal
If the input on A is larger than the input on B, we can say A is greater than B (A > B).
If the input on A is smaller than the input on B, we can say A is less than B (A < B).
For example, you are required to complete 8 hours of class a day. You can only go home once your total hours in class
Using a comparator circuit will tell you if you can go home. Let A equal the number of hours you have been in class. Let B equal 8 hours.
If A is greater than B, you have worked overtime go home!
If A is equal to B, - you have put in your 8 hours, go home.
If A is less than B, - you must stay and complete 8 hours.
The comparator circuit only recognizes a difference, not the amount of difference.

A comparator circuit wouldn't be very useful if you could only compare single digit numbers.
A four bit binary comparator uses four one bit comparators to compare 4-digit numbers...
An additional logic circuit is added to the 4 bit comparator to control the order of comparison from the Most Significant Digit (MSD) to the Least Significant Digit (LSD).
An additional logic circuit is added to the 4 bit comparator to control the order of comparison from the Most Significant Digit (MSD) to the Least Significant Digit (LSD).
MSD - Most Significant Digit
DEFINITION
LSD - Least Significant Digit
DEFINITION
If the 4 bit comparator is required to compare two numbers, comparator 1 looks at the MSD of each number.
If the MSD on A is greater than the MSD on B, the comparison stops and A > B is set HIGH.
If the MSD of A is less than the MSD of B, the comparison stops and A < B is set HIGH.
If the MSD on A is equal to the MSD on B, the comparison continues to the next digit and is compared in comparator 2.

If A = B in comparator 2, the comparison continues to the next comparator until the logic circuit is able to determine one of the three possible conditions. (A > B, A = B, A < B) Since A < B in comparator 2, the comparison stops and A < B is set high...
The outputs of comparators 1, 2 and 3 are A = B. The output of comparator 4 determines the result of the comparison.
